expected_structural_delta: Two runtime files change (one shared validator/export and one composable call site) plus two focused test files; no new runtime owner, state, dependency, API, persistence, or generated artifact.
minimum_design: Add one shared redirect URI parser and validator in web/src/utils/authorizationScopes.ts, route useAuthorizationLink and callback URL construction through it, and cover accepted and rejected schemes and hosts with focused tests.
outcome: G1: When an API-key authorization request carries an attacker-controlled redirect URI, the webGUI must never navigate to an attacker-controlled script URL on Cancel or success; valid HTTPS and exact localhost HTTP callbacks remain usable.

reuse_decisions.name: Existing URL parsing in authorizationScopes.ts
reuse_decisions.rationale: buildCallbackUrl already owns callback URL construction, so the existing utility remains the single policy owner.

reuse_decisions.name: useAuthorizationLink redirect validation
reuse_decisions.rationale: Route the existing computed guard through the shared validator instead of duplicating redirect policy.

reuse_decisions.name: ApiKeyAuthorize.standalone.vue navigation
reuse_decisions.rationale: Cancel and success already gate navigation through hasValidRedirectUri and buildCallbackUrl.

reuse_decisions.name: Legacy webgui StartCommand.php
reuse_decisions.rationale: The full legacy exploit chain was not independently reproduced and is a separate integration surface.
